steps.text: Heat olive oil and butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir in the onion, and cook until it has caramelized to a dark, golden brown, about 15 minutes. Stir in the balsamic vinegar, and cook for 1 minute before stirring in the chicken bouillon and cream. Bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat and stir in the Parmesan cheese until melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Cream Sauce
raw_recipe.description: The vinegar and cream go very well together. Best when sauteed chicken and asparagus is added to the mix.
raw_recipe.name: Balsamic Cream Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Heat olive oil and butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir in the onion, and cook until it has caramelized to a dark, golden brown, about 15 minutes. Stir in the balsamic vinegar, and cook for 1 minute before stirring in the chicken bouillon and cream. Bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat and stir in the Parmesan cheese until melted.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good and easy sauce. It reheats well too. For a fast meal, I make the "A Good Easy Garlic Chicken" in the pan first and then this sauce. I serve the chicken and sauce over whatever pasta I have on-hand. The only thing I do different is to 1/2 the chicken bouillon and leave the sauce on the burner while stirring in the parm. cheese. It's a definite keeper! *UPDATE* I've made this 3 times (w/the chicken) and each time it leaves me wanting to lick the bowl clean.

I used cheddar cheese and a red onion. Also, before sautéing the onion, I cooked some Italian sausage in the pan and cooked the onion, balsamic vinegar and bouillon in some of the drippings from the sausage.

Just made this tonight. Delish! I pounded chicken breast thin and covered with salt pepper and garlic powder. Cooked off chicken with olive oil and set aside to rest under foil. Used the same pan for the cream sauce as directed, with the exception of one garlic clove, diced. Scraping the bits off the bottom of the pan fished sauce and put chicken back into pan and covered with sauce. Served with egg noodle pasta. Omg, definitely a keeper!

This is an amazing dish that I've used many times over pasta and sometimes even over london broil (it's delicious). I add a whole onion because I like onions and I don't mince them I cut them thickly. Sometimes my guests don't like onions so it's easy for them to pick out. I also throw in some mushrooms at the beginning with the onions adds a deeper flavor. Sometimes that I've made it I have substituted the heavy cream for a bechamel sauce (1 cup milk + 1-2 T flour). I add the flour to the butter, onions, and mushrooms after they have cooked, then add the milk at the end. The sauce isn't as thick, which have been the only complaints.

Used ingredients on hand: Substituted 1 diced leek for onion, part of 1 packet vegetable flavored Swanson's "Flavor Boost" for bullion cubes, added chopped prosciutto after leeks had sautéed to golden brown, then proceeded with a sweet balsamic vinegar per rest of recipe. Served over hearty Penne Rigate pasta and garnished with capers. Easy, delicious, fairly quick, forgiving and interchangeable ingredients. Family raved over it.

This was very good! I added 1 tablespoon of flour before adding the vinegar as a thickener because I used fat free milk. Also I used a 1/2 of a vegetable broth cube instead of chicken bouillon. Easy sauce to make and delicious even with my changes.

Delicious and lovely sauce! I made a few changes which worked out well: used shallots instead of onions, mixed 1 tblsp of corn starch with milk added that to 1/2 cup of milk in addition to the cream, and added 2 cloves of garlic to the sauce. Also skipped the ckn bouillon granules and doubled the balsamic vinegar & cheese. I mixed the sauce with fresh garlic linguine pasta mixed with sauteed spinach, mushroom, onions, and peppers.

Excellent! I doubled the recipe, added some cut up chicken breast that I browned in oil in another pan, and used 1/2 c. cream and 1/2 c. milk instead of all cream. Turned out terrific! Even my picky 10-year-old loved it!

This was absolutely delicious! I added a clove of garlic, pressed, at the end of carmelizing the onions, used chicken base instead of granules, and added sauteed chicken breast and asparagus. I used Romano instead of Parmesan, freshly grated, and added it a little at a time. At the end of stirring it in, it seemed to be a little stringy, so I stirred in a tablespoon or so of the liquid that had collected in the pan when I sauteed the chicken and asparagus pieces, and that loosened it up nicely. All in all, I will DEFINITELY be making this one again!

Fantastic sauce. I added chopped mushrooms,and lots of sliced garlic, and topped with fresh minced parsley. My son said mix half the sauce into the pasta and pour the rest over the top. Loved it - even using 1/2 cream and 1/2 milk. Update: w/2 lbs pasta I use 1/2 c olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 1 cup balsamic vinegar, 3 lrg portabello mushrooms chopped, 6 T chicken bullion, 1 qt milk, 3 c heavy cream, 2 8-oz pkgs Sargento parmesan. LOVE IT for 12-16 people!!!!

OUTSTANDING! Simple, different, and so impressive. I used half and half instead of cream, and added garlic and basil. Made a double batch so I would have leftovers, but my boyfriend loved it so much the extra never made it to the fridge. I'll definitely make this again, and will add fresh mushrooms next time.

Just a tip... Be sure to use a good balsamic and cook it until it starts to reduce. This will cut the strong acidic flavor and bring out the sweetness. And if you have trouble mixing the grated parm into the sauce, skip the canned stuff and grate it yourself. Makes a world of difference.
We've been making this recipe for years - we actually use it as a steak sauce. It's a huge hit!
No changes. My partner complimented me two times on the sauce, which I served over a boneless chicken breast from a rotisserie chicken and white rice with peas. Delicious.

I've been using this recipe for about 10 years now (I think?) and it's absolutely delicious. Simple yet full of flavor, usually the ingredients are on hand. Tonight I actually subbed red wine vinegar for most of the balsamic because I only had about a tsp of balsamic, and I added some cream cheese since I only had milk instead of cream, but it was still amazing. I always double the onion and I usually add garlic, but the base recipe is gold medal worthy on its own!

Very flavorful, made enough for leftovers from 50g needed for pan-fried chicken livers, which were excellent. Will DEFINITELY make this again! 1 tsp of chicken bouillon instead of 2 also. **don't thicken with flour as a reviewer suggested, good as is
This is an excellent sauce for chicken. I make this recipe often by request of my son. I usually make it with asparagus stuffed chicken breast. This is definitely a keeper.
Love it - didn't have any onion, so I used garlic instead. I completed it with asparagus, penne and sun-dried tomatoes. Delicious!
I followed the recipe exactly, as a sauce for the “Easy Garlic Chicken” recipe. My husband kept saying “Wow, hon!”
Wonderful flavor on prosciutto and cheese tortellini.
Tasted great with dark balsamic and Irish cheddar
